Copyright protects a program’s code, Grimmelmann says, but not the algorithms and ideas the code implements. “This opens up a whole world of mods and remixes and interoperable new clients that really reduce the lead time people get from deploying software,” he says.
paras.zh: 对于软件行业的某些领域来说，这是一个法律无法轻易解决的生存问题。格里梅尔曼说，版权保护程序的代码，但不保护代码实现的算法和想法。 “这开启了一个模组、混音和可互操作的新客户端的世界，真正减少了人们部署软件的准备时间，”他说。

paras.en: REA isn’t the only thing eating into that head start. In early October Anthropic’s Claude Opus 5.5 helped a developer build open-source clones of Adobe’s Creative Cloud programs, which are known for their tight controls and steep prices.
paras.zh: REA isn’t the only thing eating into that head start. 10 月初，Anthropic 的 Claude Opus 5.5 帮助开发人员构建了 Adob​​e Creative Cloud 程序的开源克隆，该程序以其严格的控制和高昂的价格而闻名。

paras.en: Joey Castillo, an open-source developer and technologist in residence at Cornell Tech, went after something smaller. He has reverse engineered various tools in the past, but his first brush with using AI to do it came when he tried to modify a smart ring he had bought in Shenzhen, China. He was impressed that the AI model could reverse engineer the ring and teach him at the same time. “I learned a lot just by watching Claude work,” he says.
paras.zh: Joey Castillo 是康奈尔科技大学的一名开源开发人员和技术专家，他追求的是更小的东西。他过去曾对各种工具进行逆向工程，但当他试图修改他在中国深圳购买的智能戒指时，他第一次接触到使用人工智能来实现这一点。令他印象深刻的是，人工智能模型可以对戒指进行逆向工程，同时教他。 “通过观看克劳德工作，我学到了很多东西，”他说。

paras.en: The desire to tinker comes from wanting to take control of the things you buy, according to Castillo. “I bought this object, and it’s being gatekept from me,” he says. “Now I’m going to have the power to make it do what I want.”
paras.zh: 卡斯蒂略表示，修补的欲望来自于想要控制你所购买的东西。 “我买了这个东西，但它却被我看守着，”他说。 “现在我将有能力让它做我想做的事。”

paras.en: Some of those gates serve an important purpose, though. Much as AI is proving adept at breaking into security systems, it is also very good at breaking things like digital rights management and the protected firmware baked into devices.
paras.zh: 不过，其中一些大门有重要的用途。正如人工智能被证明擅长闯入安全系统一样，它也非常擅长破坏数字版权管理和设备中受保护的固件等内容。

paras.en: Projects like REA may also make it too easy for amateurs to gain a sort of synthetic expertise. Castillo and his open-source friends worry about people digging around in devices they don’t fully understand. “This is all going to be very fun and games until someone vibe codes firmware and it causes the battery to catch fire midflight,” Castillo says. He doubts AI models have the foresight that reverse engineering experts bring to deciding which modifications to make because AI “can only ‘yes, and.’ It can’t ‘no, but.’”
paras.zh: 像 REA 这样的项目也可能让业余爱好者很容易获得某种综合专业知识。卡斯蒂略和他的开源朋友担心人们在他们不完全理解的设备上进行挖掘。卡斯蒂略说：“这一切都将非常有趣和游戏，直到有人对固件进行编码并导致电池在飞行中着火。”他怀疑人工智能模型是否具有逆向工程专家那样的远见来决定进行哪些修改，因为人工智能“只能说‘是，并且’。而不能说‘不，但是’。”

paras.en: Since our first conversation with Morluto, some social media users have reported OpenAI and Anthropic banning or blocking their use of REA. In a reply on X, an OpenAI researcher called the block on reverse engineering “mostly accidental.”
paras.zh: 自从我们第一次与 Morluto 交谈以来，一些社交媒体用户报告了 OpenAI 和 Anthropic 禁止或阻止他们使用 REA。在 X 上的回复中，一位 OpenAI 研究人员称逆向工程受阻“主要是偶然的”。

paras.en: Morluto isn’t worried. If anything, he says, the “fiasco” just brings more attention to the project and to the kind of discovery he was aiming for. “That’s the core of Reverse Engineer Anything,” he says. “It’s a road that leads you to question what it is that you want.”
paras.zh: 莫鲁托并不担心。他说，如果说有什么不同的话，那就是“惨败”只会让更多人关注这个项目以及他所追求的发现。 “这就是逆向工程的核心，”他说。 “这是一条让你质疑自己想要什么的道路。”

paras.en: Accidental or not, such obstacles are unlikely to stop people who really want to reverse engineer their devices. Castillo already has a fallback in GLM-5.3, an open-weight model from the Chinese company Z.ai. Once it’s downloaded, no one can take it away. “If Anthropic and OpenAI decide they’re going to ban my account for reverse engineering, I’m going to fire up GLM-5.3 and reverse engineer the smart ring,” he says, “because I think it’s really cool to make this thing do what I wanted.”
paras.zh: 不管是否偶然，这些障碍不太可能阻止那些真正想要对其设备进行逆向工程的人。 Castillo 已经有了 GLM-5.3 的后备方案，这是中国公司 Z.ai 的开放权重模型。一旦下载，任何人都无法将其带走。 “如果 Anthropic 和 OpenAI 决定禁止我的逆向工程账户，我就会启动 GLM-5.3 并对智能环进行逆向工程，”他说，“因为我认为让这个东西做我想做的事情真的很酷。”

articles.title: Why do flamingos dance while they eat? This scientist found out
articles.author: Anna Mattson

paras.en: On a family trip to Atlanta, Víctor Ortega Jiménez spent time taking pictures and videos of flamingos as they fed in their pond. It wasn’t to admire their long legs or flamboyant pink color. Instead, he noticed the “beautiful” ripples spreading across the water as the birds ate under the surface. But he didn’t know why the waves were happening.
paras.zh: 在一次前往亚特兰大的家庭旅行中，维克多·奥尔特加·希门尼斯 (Víctor Ortega Jiménez) 花时间拍摄了火烈鸟在池塘里进食的照片和视频。这并不是为了欣赏他们的长腿或艳丽的粉色。相反，他注意到当鸟类在水面下进食时，“美丽”的涟漪在水面上蔓延。但他不知道为什么会出现波浪。

paras.en: It took “more than four years to answer that question,” says Ortega Jiménez, of the University of California, Berkeley. “But I think the answer was fascinating.”
paras.zh: 加州大学伯克利分校的奥尔特加·希门尼斯说，“花了四年多的时间才回答这个问题”。 “但我认为答案很有趣。”

paras.en: Ortega Jiménez’s focus is biomechanics, or the study of how mechanics applies to animal movement and structure. His goal is to understand how animal behaviors might lead to human-made engineering feats.
paras.zh: 奥尔特加·希门尼斯的研究重点是生物力学，即研究力学如何应用于动物运动和结构。他的目标是了解动物行为如何导致人造工程壮举。

paras.en: He discovered that, by retracting their heads, flamingos produce vortexlike traps with water to scoop up algae. They stomp around — or dance, if you will — amplifying the vortex. The series of motions brings the food to their crooked beaks. The beaks then filter in food, releasing silt and mud.
paras.zh: 他发现，通过缩回头部，火烈鸟会用水产生漩涡状的陷阱来舀起藻类。他们跺脚——或者跳舞，如果你愿意的话——放大了漩涡。这一系列动作将食物送到它们弯曲的嘴里。然后喙过滤食物，释放淤泥和泥土。

paras.en: The impressive process can weed out particles the size of a single cell. This kind of self-cleaning filter for extremely small particles can be applied to remove microplastics and so-called forever chemicals called PFAS from water, Ortega Jiménez says.
paras.zh: 这个令人印象深刻的过程可以清除单个细胞大小的颗粒。 Ortega Jiménez 表示，这种针对极小颗粒的自清洁过滤器可用于去除水中的微塑料和所谓的永久化学物质 PFAS。

paras.en: “Nature is always full of secrets,” he says. “And I think that’s the riddle that keeps me going, trying to understand nature. That’s my way to see science: by observation and trying to be inspired and trying to solve a problem.”
paras.zh: “大自然总是充满秘密，”他说。 “我认为这就是让我继续前进、努力理解自然的谜团。这就是我看待科学的方式：通过观察、试图受到启发并试图解决问题。”

articles.title: Three-quarters of NFL football players may end up with CTE
articles.author: Aimee Cunningham

paras.en: An estimated three-quarters of NFL players who died in a 16-year period had the devastating neurogenerative disease called CTE.
paras.zh: 据估计，在 16 年内死亡的 NFL 球员中有四分之三患有名为 CTE 的破坏性神经再生疾病。

paras.en: Back in 2017, researchers reported that an estimated 99 percent of former NFL players developed CTE, or chronic traumatic encephalopathy, from an analysis of donated brains. But the families who provided the donations may have done so because their football-playing relatives had symptoms related to CTE, which could skew the results. A new study, which accounts for this potential bias, estimates that nearly 75 percent of former NFL players have CTE at death. It’s the first population-level estimate for NFL players, researchers report October 28 in JAMA Network Open.
paras.zh: 早在 2017 年，研究人员就报告称，根据对捐赠大脑的分析，估计 99% 的前 NFL 球员患有 CTE（慢性创伤性脑病）。但提供捐款的家庭可能这样做是因为他们踢足球的亲戚有与 CTE 相关的症状，这可能会扭曲结果。一项新的研究解释了这种潜在的偏差，估计近 75% 的前 NFL 球员在死亡时患有 CTE。研究人员于 10 月 28 日在 JAMA Network Open 上报告称，这是对 NFL 球员的首次人口水平估计。

paras.en: The development of CTE is linked to repeated blows to the head over time. The disease can occur in people who play contact sports, experience intimate partner violence or engage in military combat. A study of American football players suggests that the longer the duration of repeated head trauma, the higher the risk of CTE and the more severe the condition. During life, people who are later diagnosed with CTE can experience symptoms including memory issues, difficulty concentrating, depression and poor impulse control.
paras.zh: CTE 的发生与头部反复受到打击有关。这种疾病可能发生在从事接触性运动、遭受亲密伴侣暴力或参加军事战斗的人身上。一项针对美国橄榄球运动员的研究表明，反复头部外伤的持续时间越长，发生 CTE 的风险就越高，病情也越严重。在生活中，后来被诊断出患有 CTE 的人可能会出现记忆问题、注意力难以集中、抑郁和冲动控制能力差等症状。

paras.en: A brain protein called tau, which usually helps nerve cells communicate and performs other jobs, goes awry in CTE. Brains with the disease are snarled with irregular, damaging clumps of the protein. The condition is diagnosed after death, during an autopsy, and has been identified most frequently among American football players.
paras.zh: 一种名为 tau 的大脑蛋白通常帮助神经细胞沟通并执行其他工作，但在 CTE 中却出现了问题。患有这种疾病的大脑中充满了不规则的、具有破坏性的蛋白质团块。这种情况是在死后通过尸检被诊断出来的，并且在美国橄榄球运动员中最常见。

paras.en: The new study, by a Boston University research team, included all previous NFL players who passed away from January 2008 through December 2023. The more than 2,300 players included almost 400 with samples in the university’s UNITE Brain Bank, with the remainder identified from records in the U.S. National Death Index. The research team determined that families of NFL players who had CTE-related symptoms in life were five times more likely to donate their relative’s brain than families whose relative did not experience symptoms. Taking that into consideration, the team landed on a population-level CTE estimate for NFL players of 74.5 percent.
paras.zh: 波士顿大学研究小组进行的这项新研究涵盖了 2008 年 1 月至 2023 年 12 月期间去世的所有 NFL 球员。这 2,300 多名球员中包括近 400 名球员，样本保存在该大学的 UNITE 脑库中，其余的则从美国国家死亡指数的记录中确定。研究小组确定，在生活中出现 CTE 相关症状的 NFL 球员的家庭捐献其亲属大脑的可能性是其亲属没有出现症状的家庭的五倍。考虑到这一点，该团队对 NFL 球员的人口水平 CTE 估计为 74.5%。

paras.en: The research team notes that determining the true prevalence of CTE is important to understanding the public health impact of the disease.
paras.zh: 研究小组指出，确定 CTE 的真实患病率对于了解该疾病对公共健康的影响非常重要。

articles.title: A proof-of-concept test can spot bladder cancer in urine
articles.author: Meghan Rosen

paras.en: A splash of pee could reveal bladder cancer.
paras.zh: 尿液飞溅可能会发现膀胱癌。

paras.en: Using a proof-of-concept urine test that decodes RNA molecules, it’s possible to pick out patients with the disease, scientists report October 2 in Nature Medicine. Because urine is in direct contact with bladder tumors, it’s “a very attractive fluid” to look for this type of cancer, says Stanford University oncologist Maximilian Diehn. The technology, still in its infancy, offers a glimpse of what future screening tests might entail.
paras.zh: 科学家于 10 月 2 日在《自然·医学》杂志上报告称，使用解码 RNA 分子的概念验证尿液测试，可以挑选出患有这种疾病的患者。斯坦福大学肿瘤学家马克西米利安·迪恩 (Maximilian Diehn) 表示，由于尿液与膀胱肿瘤直接接触，因此它是寻找此类癌症的“非常有吸引力的液体”。这项技术仍处于起步阶段，可以让我们了解未来筛查测试可能需要的内容。

paras.en: Today’s liquid biopsies for cancer, which examine bodily fluids rather than tissue samples, largely focus on finding DNA that tumors shed into the blood. Diehn’s lab sought a different stream of information. The researchers analyzed RNA, DNA’s molecular cousin. RNA isn’t as stable as DNA, so it hasn’t been researchers’ top target. But it carries info that DNA lacks, such as which genes are turned on. That’s important, Diehn says, “because it can tell you what the cancer is doing at any given moment.”
paras.zh: 如今的癌症液体活检主要检查的是体液而不是组织样本，主要侧重于寻找肿瘤脱落到血液中的 DNA。迪恩的实验室寻求不同的信息流。研究人员分析了 DNA 的近亲分子 RNA。 RNA 不如 DNA 稳定，因此它并不是研究人员的首要目标。但它携带 DNA 所缺乏的信息，例如哪些基因被打开。迪恩说，这很重要，“因为它可以告诉你癌症在任何特定时刻正在做什么。”

paras.en: Diehn and his colleagues previously developed a technique to analyze dribs of RNA floating in blood. In samples from people with lung cancer, the team could read RNA signatures of the disease. Now, the researchers have shown that their technique is a whiz at detecting cancer in urine. The team tested their technique using samples from 515 cancer patients and healthy people. It was sensitive enough to identify 95 out of 100 people with bladder cancer — even at early stages of disease. What’s more, the test also offered hints about cancer biology, such as the type of tumor and risk of recurrence. Those details could help doctors make decisions about treatments, Diehn says.
paras.zh: Diehn 和他的同事之前开发了一种技术来分析血液中漂浮的 RNA 颗粒。在肺癌患者的样本中，研究小组可以读取该疾病的 RNA 特征。现在，研究人员已经证明他们的技术在检测尿液中的癌症方面非常出色。该团队使用 515 名癌症患者和健康人的样本测试了他们的技术。它的灵敏度足够高，即使在疾病的早期阶段，也能识别出 100 名膀胱癌患者中的 95 名。此外，该测试还提供了有关癌症生物学的提示，例如肿瘤类型和复发风险。迪恩说，这些细节可以帮助医生做出治疗决定。

paras.en: The researchers are now exploring their technique’s potential for picking up other cancers. Their evidence suggests that it can spot cancer in the kidney and prostate, organs also washed by urine. One day, Diehn says, he can imagine a multi-cancer urine test focused on tumors in the genitourinary tract. But there’s much to do before such a test makes it into clinics.
paras.zh: 研究人员现在正在探索他们的技术检测其他癌症的潜力。他们的证据表明，它可以发现肾脏和前列腺中的癌症，这些器官也被尿液清洗过。迪恩说，有一天，他可以想象一种针对泌尿生殖道肿瘤的多种癌症尿液检测。但在这种测试进入临床之前还有很多工作要做。

paras.en: Because the technology is so new, the jury’s still out on whether RNA-based testing will find use in cancer screening, Diehn says. “But absolutely, I think the field needs to investigate it.”
paras.zh: Diehn 表示，由于这项技术太新，基于 RNA 的检测是否能用于癌症筛查尚无定论。 “但绝对，我认为该领域需要对此进行调查。”

articles.title: Humans in The Andes Seem to Have Evolved an Unusual Genetic Ability
articles.author: Michelle Starr

paras.en: Over thousands of years, humans living high in the Argentinian Andes have relied on drinking water that would make most people deathly ill.
paras.zh: 数千年来，生活在阿根廷安第斯山脉高处的人类一直依赖饮用水，而这会使大多数人患上致命疾病。

paras.en: There, naturally occurring arsenic in volcanic bedrock leaches into the groundwater, contaminating the local water supply with levels of the toxic metalloid that would pose serious health risks to most human populations.
paras.zh: 在那里，火山基岩中天然存在的砷渗入地下水，污染了当地的供水，其有毒类金属含量对大多数人构成严重的健康风险。

paras.en: But for one group in northern Argentina, natural selection may have provided an unusual genetic advantage, research shows.
paras.zh: 但研究表明，对于阿根廷北部的一个群体来说，自然选择可能提供了一种不同寻常的遗传优势。

paras.en: According to a DNA analysis of people across western South America, a population in the Argentinian Andes carries a gene variant that likely helps them metabolize arsenic more safely.
paras.zh: 根据对南美洲西部人群的 DNA 分析，阿根廷安第斯山脉的人群携带一种基因变异，可能有助于他们更安全地代谢砷。

paras.en: "Adaptation drives genomic changes; however, evidence of specific adaptations in humans remains limited," researchers wrote in a 2015 study led by evolutionary biologists Carina Schlebusch and Lucie Gattepaille of Uppsala University.
paras.zh: 研究人员在乌普萨拉大学进化生物学家 Carina Schlebusch 和 Lucie Gattepaille 领导的 2015 年研究中写道：“适应推动了基因组变化；然而，人类特定适应的证据仍然有限。”

paras.en: "Our data show that adaptation to tolerate the environmental stressor arsenic has likely driven an increase in the frequencies of protective variants of AS3MT, providing the first evidence of human adaptation to a toxic chemical."
paras.zh: “我们的数据显示，对环境应激源砷的适应可能导致 AS3MT 保护性变体频率的增加，这提供了人类适应有毒化学物质的第一个证据。”

paras.en: Given enough time and gentle enough exposure to a hazard, life has shown a remarkable ability to adapt to all sorts of wild conditions – from extreme heat to complete lack of oxygen to dangerous radiation levels.
paras.zh: 如果有足够的时间和足够温和地暴露在危险中，生命就表现出了适应各种野生条件的非凡能力——从极端炎热到完全缺氧，再到危险的辐射水平。

paras.en: However, relatively little is known about how human populations adapt to toxic chemicals in their environment. Arsenic is highly toxic, associated with cancer, skin lesions, pregnancy complications, and early death.
paras.zh: 然而，人们对于人类如何适应环境中的有毒化学物质知之甚少。砷具有剧毒，与癌症、皮肤损伤、妊娠并发症和过早死亡有关。

paras.en: It's also widespread, naturally present at high levels in the groundwater of many regions around the world.
paras.zh: 它也广泛存在，在世界许多地区的地下水中自然存在高含量。

paras.en: The current recommended limit for arsenic in drinking water, set by the World Health Organization, is 10 micrograms per liter.
paras.zh: 世界卫生组织目前建议的饮用水中砷含量限值为每升 10 微克。

paras.en: Until a filtration system was installed in 2012, the remote, high-altitude town of San Antonio de los Cobres, in Argentina's Puna de Atacama plateau, had drinking water that contained around 200 micrograms of arsenic per liter – about 20 times the recommended limit.
paras.zh: 在 2012 年安装过滤系统之前，位于阿根廷阿塔卡马高原的偏远高海拔小镇圣安东尼奥德洛斯科布雷斯的饮用水中砷含量约为每升 200 微克，约为建议限值的 20 倍。

paras.en: Yet the region has been inhabited for thousands of years – at least 7,000 years, and perhaps as long as 11,000.
paras.zh: 然而，该地区已经有人居住了数千年——至少 7,000 年，也许长达 11,000 年。

paras.en: This apparent ability to shrug off dangerously high arsenic levels puzzled scientists for decades.
paras.zh: 这种摆脱危险的高砷含量的明显能力让科学家们困惑了几十年。

paras.en: In 1995, scientists noted that women from the Argentinian Andes had a "unique" ability to metabolize arsenic, as evidenced by metabolites in their urine.
paras.zh: 1995年，科学家指出，阿根廷安第斯山脉的女性具有“独特”的砷代谢能力，她们尿液中的代谢物就证明了这一点。

paras.en: When arsenic enters the body, enzymes convert it through several chemical forms.
paras.zh: 当砷进入体内时，酶会将其转化为几种化学形式。

paras.en: One of these intermediate forms, called monomethylated arsenic (MMA), is particularly toxic. A later form, dimethylated arsenic (DMA), is easier for the body to excrete in urine.
paras.zh: 其中一种中间体形式称为单甲基化砷（MMA），毒性特别大。后来的形式，二甲基化砷（DMA），更容易被身体通过尿液排出。

paras.en: People in San Antonio de los Cobres tended to produce less of the toxic intermediate and more of the easily excreted form, suggesting their bodies were unusually efficient at processing arsenic.
paras.zh: 圣安东尼奥德洛斯科布雷斯的人们倾向于产生较少的有毒中间体和更多易于排泄的形式，这表明他们的身体在处理砷方面异常有效。

paras.en: Intrigued, Schlebusch, Gattepaille, and their colleagues wanted to solve the puzzle at the genetic level.
paras.zh: 出于好奇，施勒布施、加特佩尔和他们的同事希望在基因水平上解决这个难题。

paras.en: The team analyzed DNA from blood samples or cheek swabs, taken from 124 women in San Antonio de los Cobres whose urine showed a wide range of arsenic metabolite levels.
paras.zh: 研究小组分析了圣安东尼奥德洛斯科布雷斯 124 名女性的血液样本或脸颊拭子中的 DNA，这些女性的尿液中砷代谢物水平存在很大差异。

paras.en: They then examined millions of genetic markers across the genome.
paras.zh: 然后他们检查了基因组中数百万个遗传标记。

paras.en: To determine whether the gene variant was unique to the Argentine population, the researchers compared their results with publicly available genome data from Peru and Colombia, drawn from the international 1000 Genomes Project.
paras.zh: 为了确定该基因变异是否是阿根廷人口所独有的，研究人员将他们的结果与来自国际千人基因组计划的秘鲁和哥伦比亚的公开基因组数据进行了比较。

paras.en: Previous research showed that an enzyme called arsenic (+3 oxidation state) methyltransferase (AS3MT) could play a key role in arsenic metabolism, so that is where the researchers focused their efforts.
paras.zh: 先前的研究表明，一种名为砷（+3氧化态）甲基转移酶（AS3MT）的酶可能在砷代谢中发挥关键作用，因此这就是研究人员的重点工作。

paras.en: What they found was a cluster of genetic variants near the AS3MT gene that strongly influenced how the body processes arsenic.
paras.zh: 他们发现 AS3MT 基因附近的一组遗传变异强烈影响身体处理砷的方式。

paras.en: These variants were far more common in people from San Antonio de los Cobres than in genetically similar populations in Peru and Colombia.
paras.zh: 这些变异在圣安东尼奥德洛斯科布雷斯人中比在基因相似的秘鲁和哥伦比亚人群中更为常见。

paras.en: A September 2025 study out of the University of Chicago, looking at more than 6,500 arsenic-exposed adults in Bangladesh, identified two more gene clusters – FMO and GSTO – that also shape how efficiently someone metabolizes arsenic, on top of the AS3MT variant.
paras.zh: 芝加哥大学 2025 年 9 月的一项研究对孟加拉国 6,500 多名接触砷的成年人进行了研究，发现了另外两个基因簇——FMO 和 GSTO——除了 AS3MT 变体之外，它们也决定了某人代谢砷的效率。

paras.en: The variants appear to make the body more efficient at converting arsenic into forms that can be safely excreted in urine, reducing the buildup of the most toxic intermediate compounds – a result that neatly aligns with earlier studies of arsenic metabolites in urine.
paras.zh: 这些变体似乎使人体能够更有效地将砷转化为可以安全地通过尿液排出的形式，从而减少毒性最强的中间化合物的积累——这一结果与早期对尿液中砷代谢物的研究完全一致。

paras.en: While arsenic contamination is common around the world, very few communities have lived with such high levels of exposure for long periods of time.
paras.zh: 虽然砷污染在世界各地都很常见，但很少有社区能够长期生活在如此高水平的砷污染下。

paras.en: In San Antonio de los Cobres, people have lived with arsenic in their groundwater for thousands of years – long enough for natural selection to favor traits that reduce vulnerability to arsenic's toxic effects.
paras.zh: 在圣安东尼奥德洛斯科布雷斯，人们在地下水中含有砷的情况下生活了数千年，这段时间足以让自然选择青睐那些能够降低砷毒性影响的性状。

paras.en: Later research suggests similar genetic signals may also appear in other Andean populations exposed to arsenic for generations, supporting the findings that long-term exposure can drive genetic tolerance, and hinting that the adaptation may be more widespread across the region.
paras.zh: 后来的研究表明，类似的遗传信号也可能出现在世世代代接触砷的其他安第斯人群中，这支持了长期接触砷可以提高遗传耐受性的发现，并暗示这种适应可能在整个地区更为广泛。

paras.en: "Given the severe deleterious health effects of arsenic in both children and adults," the researchers wrote, "individuals who carry the arsenic-tolerance haplotype… could have a very strong selective advantage in high-arsenic environments."
paras.zh: 研究人员写道：“考虑到砷对儿童和成人的严重有害健康影响，携带砷耐受单倍型的个体……在高砷环境中可能具有非常强大的选择优势。”

paras.en: The research was published in Molecular Biology and Evolution.
paras.zh: 该研究发表在《分子生物学与进化》上。

articles.title: The Links Between Napping And Dementia May Go Further Than We Realized
articles.author: Peter Dockrill

paras.en: Dozing off in your armchair in the middle of the afternoon is one of life's simple pleasures.
paras.zh: 午后坐在扶手椅上打瞌睡是生活中简单的乐趣之一。

paras.en: But depending on how often you find yourself doing it, those daytime naps could be a warning sign of worsening cognitive health, research suggests.
paras.zh: 但研究表明，根据你发现自己这样做的频率，白天小睡可能是认知健康状况恶化的警告信号。

paras.en: In a new study, researchers found seniors who napped frequently were significantly more likely to develop dementia over the next decade, compared to people who rarely or never napped.
paras.zh: 在一项新的研究中，研究人员发现，与很少或从不午睡的人相比，经常午睡的老年人在未来十年内患痴呆症的可能性明显更高。

paras.en: The findings, published in The Journals of Gerontology, Series A: Biological Sciences and Medical Sciences, don't mean that napping is driving cognitive decline, but they identify napping as a risk factor for dementia that we should pay more attention to.
paras.zh: 发表在《老年学杂志 A 系列：生物科学和医学科学》上的研究结果并不意味着小睡会导致认知能力下降，但他们认为小睡是痴呆症的一个危险因素，我们应该更加关注。

paras.en: "More frequent napping could be a marker of changes in the brain, rather than a cause of brain changes that lead to dementia," says psychologist and sleep researcher Adam Spira from Johns Hopkins University.
paras.zh: 约翰·霍普金斯大学的心理学家兼睡眠研究员 Adam Spira 表示：“更频繁的小睡可能是大脑变化的标志，而不是导致痴呆的大脑变化的原因。”

paras.en: In their study, Spira and fellow researchers analyzed data from the National Health and Aging Trends Study (NHATS), a longitudinal survey of Medicare beneficiaries in the US aged 65 years and older.
paras.zh: 在他们的研究中，Spira 和其他研究人员分析了国家健康和老龄化趋势研究 (NHATS) 的数据，这是一项针对美国 65 岁及以上医疗保险受益人的纵向调查。

paras.en: The team examined data from 995 of the NHATS participants, all of whom answered questions about their napping habits as part of the research, and none of whom had probable or possible dementia at the outset of the study.
paras.zh: 研究小组检查了 995 名 NHATS 参与者的数据，作为研究的一部分，所有参与者都回答了有关他们午睡习惯的问题，并且在研究开始时没有人患有可能或可能的痴呆症。

paras.en: Over a median follow-up period of five years, 417 (41.9 percent) of the participants were classified as having developed possible or probable dementia since the commencement of the study.
paras.zh: 在中位五年的随访期内，自研究开始以来，417 名参与者（41.9%）被归类为可能患有或可能患有痴呆症。

paras.en: After adjusting for a range of potential confounding factors in the data – including age, sex, race/ethnicity, education, smoking status, body mass index, and various health conditions and sleep factors – the researchers found that frequent nappers had the highest risk of developing the condition, compared to infrequent nappers and non-nappers.
paras.zh: 在调整了数据中的一系列潜在混杂因素（包括年龄、性别、种族/民族、教育程度、吸烟状况、体重指数以及各种健康状况和睡眠因素）后，研究人员发现，与不经常打盹和不打瞌睡的人相比，经常打瞌睡的人患这种疾病的风险最高。

paras.en: Frequent nappers – people who said they napped every day or most days – had a 48 percent higher rate of dementia than people who never or rarely had naps.
paras.zh: 经常小睡的人（自称每天或大部分时间都小睡的人）比从不或很少小睡的人患痴呆症的几率高 48%。

paras.en: Unintentional napping was also associated with a greater risk of dementia (39 percent higher rate than non-nappers).
paras.zh: 无意识的小睡还与患痴呆症的风险增加有关（比不小睡的人高出 39%）。

paras.en: Length of naps was also a factor, with people who napped for 30 minutes or less having a 40 percent higher rate of dementia than non-nappers in the study period.
paras.zh: 午睡时间长短也是一个因素，在研究期间，午睡时间不超过 30 分钟的人患痴呆症的几率比不午睡的人高 40%。

paras.en: Frequent, unintentional, and shorter (30 minutes or less) napping were also found to be associated with higher risks of developing impairment in memory during follow-up, the researchers found.
paras.zh: 研究人员发现，频繁、无意识和较短（30 分钟或更短）的小睡也与随访期间出现记忆障碍的较高风险相关。

paras.en: It's worth noting the researchers also found signs of elevated dementia risk associated with infrequent napping, intentional napping, and napping for periods of 30 minutes or longer, but the effects were not statistically significant after adjustment in the final analysis.
paras.zh: 值得注意的是，研究人员还发现，痴呆风险升高的迹象与不经常午睡、有意午睡、午睡时间超过 30 分钟或更长有关，但最终分析调整后，其影响并不具有统计学意义。

paras.en: Other studies have previously explored the relationship between napping and cognitive health in older adults, but the results have been mixed, with some studies showing signs of elevated cognitive risks associated with napping, and others finding little evidence of a link.
paras.zh: 其他研究此前也探讨了老年人午睡与认知健康之间的关系，但结果好坏参半，一些研究显示出与午睡相关的认知风险升高的迹象，而另一些研究则几乎没有发现任何联系的证据。

paras.en: Due to the observational nature of the new study, the findings can't be interpreted as evidence that frequent, unintentional, or short naps cause dementia, and the researchers acknowledge that the links they've found are complicated.
paras.zh: 由于这项新研究的观察性质，研究结果不能被解释为频繁、无意识或短暂小睡会导致痴呆的证据，研究人员承认他们发现的联系很复杂。

paras.en: "As with sleep disturbances, the association between napping and dementia may be bidirectional," they write in their paper, "such that neurological changes that adversely affect cognitive function may also lead to increased daytime napping."
paras.zh: 他们在论文中写道：“与睡眠障碍一样，小睡和痴呆之间的关联可能是双向的，因此对认知功能产生不利影响的神经系统变化也可能导致白天小睡的增加。”

paras.en: In other words, if older adults start to nap a lot during the day, it could be a sign of worsening brain health – but that worsening brain health might also be making them sleepier, prompting them to doze in waking hours.
paras.zh: 换句话说，如果老年人在白天开始频繁小睡，这可能是大脑健康状况恶化的迹象，但大脑健康状况恶化也可能使他们变得更困，促使他们在醒着的时候打瞌睡。

paras.en: Another complicating factor is that daytime napping may be a compensatory mechanism, making up for sleep disturbances at night. But just as poor rest at night might induce catch-up napping in the daytime, so might napping disrupt nighttime sleep.
paras.zh: 另一个复杂的因素是，白天小睡可能是一种补偿机制，可以弥补夜间的睡眠障碍。但是，正如晚上休息不好可能会导致白天补小睡一样，小睡也可能会扰乱夜间睡眠。

paras.en: In the study, the researchers accounted for this by adjusting for other sleep-related factors (nighttime sleep duration, daytime sleepiness, and sleep apnea risk), and the results suggest that frequent napping, unintentional napping, and naps lasting 30 minutes or less remain significantly associated with an increased risk of dementia, even after accounting for these other sleep characteristics.
paras.zh: 在这项研究中，研究人员通过调整其他与睡眠相关的因素（夜间睡眠时间、白天嗜睡和睡眠呼吸暂停风险）来解释这一点，结果表明，频繁小睡、无意识小睡和持续 30 分钟或更短的小睡仍然与痴呆症风险增加显着相关，即使在考虑了这些其他睡眠特征后也是如此。

paras.en: Related: After 30 Years, FDA Approves First-Ever Drug For a Rare Neurological Disorder
paras.zh: 相关：30 年后，FDA 批准首个治疗罕见神经系统疾病的药物

paras.en: The researchers call for future studies to "disentangle" the possible bidirectionality of the napping-dementia association they've demonstrated here.
paras.zh: 研究人员呼吁未来的研究能够“解开”他们在此证明的小睡与痴呆之间可能的双向关系。

paras.en: While we don't fully understand the nature of this link, the hope is that new research might be able to solve the puzzle, which could lead to new ways to combat dementia, a disease projected to double in the US by 2060.
paras.zh: 虽然我们并不完全了解这种联系的本质，但希望新的研究能够解决这个难题，从而找到对抗痴呆症的新方法，预计到 2060 年，这种疾病在美国的发病率将翻一番。

paras.en: "Daytime napping might be another modifiable risk factor to be targeted among older adults for primary prevention of dementia, if supported by further causal evidence," the researchers write.
paras.zh: 研究人员写道：“如果有进一步的因果证据支持，白天小睡可能是老年人痴呆症一级预防的另一个可改变的风险因素。”

paras.en: "Even if this association is not causal, napping may be a useful marker of future dementia risk to guide subsequent prevention studies among high-risk populations."
paras.zh: “即使这种关联不是因果关系，小睡也可能是未来痴呆风险的有用标志，可以指导高危人群的后续预防研究。”

paras.en: The findings are reported in The Journals of Gerontology, Series A: Biological Sciences and Medical Sciences.
paras.zh: 研究结果发表在《老年学杂志 A 系列：生物科学和医学科学》上。

articles.title: Near-Death Experiences Seem to Follow Strange Rules of Shape And Color, Study Reveals
articles.author: Michelle Starr

paras.en: Of all the strange trappings associated with the near-death experience, none is so familiar as the tunnel into the light.
paras.zh: 在所有与濒死体验相关的奇怪现象中，没有一个比进入光明的隧道更熟悉的了。

paras.en: People who have skirted perilously close to the brink of death – or even beyond it for a few moments – sometimes describe moving through darkness, like a tunnel, towards a dazzling luminous portal – like a passage into elsewhere.
paras.zh: 那些危险地接近死亡边缘——甚至暂时超越死亡边缘的人，有时会描述自己穿过黑暗，就像一条隧道，走向一个耀眼的发光门户——就像一条通往别处的通道。

paras.en: It's an image so deeply embedded in popular culture that it has become a powerful symbol of the end of life.
paras.zh: 这一形象深深植根于流行文化中，已成为生命终结的有力象征。

paras.en: But not everyone who reports a near-death experience sees a tunnel. Some describe vast, luminous spaces, curved horizons, or an overwhelming sense of being surrounded by light.
paras.zh: 但并不是每个报告濒死体验的人都看到了隧道。有些描述了广阔、明亮的空间、弯曲的地平线，或者被光包围的压倒性的感觉。

paras.en: Even in spite of these differences, though, a new study has found that otherwise varying experiences of death's waiting room may have something peculiar in common.
paras.zh: 尽管存在这些差异，但一项新的研究发现，不同的死亡候诊室经历可能有一些独特的共同点。

paras.en: When researchers asked 50 people to draw maps of the spaces they remembered encountering during near-death experiences, an intriguing pattern emerged: The geometry of those spaces appeared to be linked to the colors people recalled seeing.
paras.zh: 当研究人员要求 50 个人绘制他们记得在濒死体验中遇到的空间的地图时，出现了一个有趣的模式：这些空间的几何形状似乎与人们记得看到的颜色有关。

paras.en: The findings hint that these otherworldly experiences may not be quite as unpredictable as they seem – and that their strange geometry could offer clues to what happens in the brain at the boundary between life and death.
paras.zh: 研究结果暗示，这些超凡脱俗的经历可能并不像看起来那么不可预测，而且它们奇怪的几何形状可以为了解生与死边界时大脑中发生的事情提供线索。

paras.en: Near-death experiences fascinate most people – including scientists. However, they're not easy to study. People who experience them report something intense – emotionally, personally, or spiritually – that they often struggle to articulate.
paras.zh: 濒死体验让大多数人着迷——包括科学家。然而，研究它们并不容易。经历过这种情况的人会报告一些他们常常难以表达的强烈的情感、个人或精神上的事情。

paras.en: The clinical questions posed by the standard scientific surveys are able to record some aspects of the near-death experience, but are incapable of distilling the full complexity of it down to words on a page.
paras.zh: 标准科学调查提出的临床问题能够记录濒死体验的某些方面，但无法将其全部复杂性提炼成纸上的文字。

paras.en: Although researchers have identified recurring features, such as tunnels, lights, and out-of-body sensations, comparatively little attention has been paid to the spatial structure of these experiences – or how people perceive themselves moving through them.
paras.zh: 尽管研究人员已经识别出重复出现的特征，例如隧道、灯光和灵魂出窍的感觉，但人们对这些体验的空间结构或人们如何感知自己穿过这些体验的关注相对较少。

paras.en: Neurophenomenology researcher France Lerner of the University of Haifa in Israel and colleagues wanted to approach the question in a different way – visually. They thought that asking people to draw their experiences might reveal patterns mere words could not.
paras.zh: 以色列海法大学的神经现象学研究员 France Lerner 及其同事希望以不同的方式（视觉）来解决这个问题。他们认为，要求人们画出他们的经历可能会揭示出文字无法揭示的模式。

paras.en: They recruited 50 people who reported having had near-death experiences, and asked them to reconstruct their memories in a series of guided online sessions, using a catalog of geometric pictograms to help represent the spaces they recalled.
paras.zh: 他们招募了 50 名自称有过濒死体验的人，并要求他们在一系列在线指导课程中重建记忆，使用几何象形图目录来帮助代表他们回忆起的空间。

paras.en: Participants were asked to break their experiences into separate stages, then represent the shape of each space they recalled encountering.
paras.zh: 参与者被要求将他们的经历分成不同的阶段，然后代表他们回忆中遇到的每个空间的形状。

paras.en: They were also asked to indicate where they perceived themselves to be within those spaces, how they moved through them, and what colors they remembered seeing.
paras.zh: 他们还被要求指出他们认为自己在这些空间中的位置、他们如何穿过这些空间以及他们记得看到了什么颜色。

paras.en: The researchers then compiled a database of these reconstructions and compared them, looking for similarities in the geometry of the spaces and the qualities associated with them.
paras.zh: 然后，研究人员编制了这些重建的数据库并对它们进行比较，寻找空间几何形状和与之相关的质量的相似之处。

paras.en: And despite the intensely personal nature of the experiences, certain shapes kept cropping up.
paras.zh: 尽管这些经历具有强烈的个人性，但某些形状仍然不断出现。

paras.en: There were, the researchers found, four main categories – conical spaces, which included the familiar tunnel; broad, curved spaces, like archways; flatter, more gently curving spaces; and spaces that seemed to surround the observer completely, like the inside of a sphere or oval.
paras.zh: 研究人员发现，有四个主要类别：圆锥形空间，其中包括熟悉的隧道；宽阔、弯曲的空间，如拱门；更平坦、更柔和弯曲的空间；以及似乎完全包围观察者的空间，就像球体或椭圆形的内部。

paras.en: But the most intriguing pattern wasn't in the shapes alone – it was in the colors the study participants associated with them.
paras.zh: 但最有趣的图案不仅仅在于形状，还在于研究参与者与之相关的颜色。

paras.en: Of the 28 conical spaces reconstructed by participants, 22 were achromatic – perceived in black, white, gray, or light without discernible color.
paras.zh: 在参与者重建的 28 个圆锥形空间中，有 22 个是消色差的——以黑色、白色、灰色或浅色感知，没有可辨别的颜色。

paras.en: By contrast, 27 of the 31 broad, curved spaces were perceived in color.
paras.zh: 相比之下，31 个宽阔、弯曲的空间中有 27 个被感知为颜色。

paras.en: The other two geometric categories showed a mixture of colorful and colorless experiences, but the contrast between the tunnels and the broad, curved spaces was particularly striking.
paras.zh: 另外两个几何类别展示了彩色和无色体验的混合，但隧道和宽阔、弯曲的空间之间的对比尤其引人注目。

paras.en: That relationship – between shapes and color – could offer clues to the perceptual processes underlying these eerie experiences.
paras.zh: 这种形状和颜色之间的关系可以为这些怪异体验背后的感知过程提供线索。

paras.en: According to Lerner and her colleagues, neurological and perceptual research has already documented some similar visual relationships.
paras.zh: 勒纳和她的同事表示，神经学和知觉研究已经记录了一些类似的视觉关系。

paras.en: One example is tunnel vision, which can occur when the supply of oxygen to the retina or brain is disrupted, restricting the field of vision.
paras.zh: 一个例子是隧道视觉，当视网膜或大脑的氧气供应受到干扰，限制视野时，就会发生这种情况。

paras.en: The predominance of black, white, and gray in the tunnel-like spaces also has a possible parallel in ordinary vision. In low-light conditions, our eyes become less sensitive to color as the light-sensitive cells responsible for seeing in dim conditions take over.
paras.zh: 隧道般的空间中黑、白、灰的主导地位在普通视觉中也可能有相似之处。在弱光条件下，我们的眼睛对颜色的敏感度降低，因为负责在昏暗条件下看东西的光敏细胞接管了工作。

paras.en: Meanwhile, some of the more expansive, enveloping spaces recalled by participants bear similarities to a phenomenon called the Ganzfeld effect, in which an unchanging, blank visual field can give rise to unusual perceptual experiences, including hallucinations.
paras.zh: 与此同时，参与者回忆起的一些更广阔、更具包容性的空间与一种称为甘兹菲尔德效应的现象有相似之处，在这种现象中，不变的空白视野会产生不寻常的感知体验，包括幻觉。

paras.en: These similarities don't establish what caused the participants' experiences, however.
paras.zh: 然而，这些相似之处并不能确定是什么导致了参与者的经历。

paras.en: The researchers emphasize that their study was designed to describe and compare the recalled spaces, not identify the mechanisms responsible for them.
paras.zh: 研究人员强调，他们的研究旨在描述和比较回忆的空间，而不是确定造成这些空间的机制。

paras.en: There are also some important limitations.
paras.zh: 还有一些重要的限制。

paras.en: The participants were a relatively small, self-selected group, and they reconstructed experiences from memories that, in some cases, were many years old.
paras.zh: 参与者是一个相对较小的、自我选择的群体，他们根据记忆重建经验，在某些情况下，这些记忆是很多年前的。

paras.en: Moreover, although the geometric pictograms were based on earlier research, presenting participants with a selection of shapes may have influenced how they reconstructed their experiences. The researchers also guided the sessions, which may have introduced subtle biases.
paras.zh: 此外，虽然几何象形图是基于早期的研究，但向参与者提供一系列形状的选择可能会影响他们重建经验的方式。研究人员还指导了这些会议，这可能会引入微妙的偏见。

paras.en: Finally, without a comparison group reconstructing other kinds of unusual experiences, it's impossible to know whether these geometric patterns are unique to near-death experiences.
paras.zh: 最后，如果没有对照组重建其他类型的不寻常经历，就不可能知道这些几何图案是否是濒死体验所独有的。

paras.en: Still, the patterns that emerged from visually recording recollections of the experience reveal something that previous research has largely overlooked – suggesting that tapping into the uncanny may require asking questions in a different kind of language.
paras.zh: 尽管如此，从视觉记录的经历回忆中出现的模式揭示了以前的研究在很大程度上忽视的一些东西——这表明挖掘神秘的事物可能需要用不同类型的语言提出问题。

paras.en: The research has been published in Frontiers in Psychology.
paras.zh: 该研究已发表在《心理学前沿》上。

articles.title: Scientists use sound waves to deliver a new attack on deadly brain cancer

paras.en: Scientists use sound waves to deliver a new attack on deadly brain cancer
paras.zh: 科学家利用声波对致命脑癌进行新的攻击

paras.en: - Scientists at the University of Virginia have developed a promising new strategy to fight glioblastoma, one of the deadliest and most difficult-to-treat forms of brain cancer. Their experimental approach combines focused ultrasound, tiny nanoparticles, and genetic molecules called microRNAs to attack multiple cancer-driving genes simultaneously.
paras.zh: - 弗吉尼亚大学的科学家们开发了一种有前景的新策略来对抗胶质母细胞瘤，胶质母细胞瘤是最致命和最难治疗的脑癌之一。他们的实验方法结合了聚焦超声波、微小纳米粒子和称为 microRNA 的遗传分子，同时攻击多个癌症驱动基因。

paras.en: Scientists at the University of Virginia Comprehensive Cancer Center have developed a promising experimental strategy for treating glioblastoma, the most common and aggressive malignant brain tumor in adults. The new approach could help overcome some of the biggest obstacles that have limited the effectiveness of existing brain cancer treatments.
paras.zh: 弗吉尼亚大学综合癌症中心的科学家们开发了一种有前途的实验策略来治疗胶质母细胞瘤，这是成人中最常见和最具侵袭性的恶性脑肿瘤。新方法可以帮助克服限制现有脑癌治疗效果的一些最大障碍。

paras.en: The research team, led by UVA's Roger Abounader, MD, PhD, identified tiny genetic molecules known as "microRNAs" that can interfere with several genes responsible for the development and growth of glioblastoma. To deliver these molecules into the brain, the researchers combined specialized nanoparticles, focused ultrasound and microscopic bubbles. Together, these technologies offer a way to temporarily cross the brain's protective barrier, which normally prevents many treatments from reaching brain tumors and other neurological conditions.
paras.zh: 由 UVA 医学博士 Roger Abounader 领导的研究小组发现了一种被称为“microRNA”的微小遗传分子，它可以干扰几个负责胶质母细胞瘤发育和生长的基因。为了将这些分子输送到大脑中，研究人员结合了特殊的纳米颗粒、聚焦超声波和微小气泡。这些技术共同提供了一种暂时跨越大脑保护屏障的方法，该屏障通常会阻止许多治疗方法到达脑肿瘤和其他神经系统疾病。

paras.en: "This new approach could help target numerous molecules that promote cancer growth, including those for which no drugs exist, at the same time to achieve better therapies," said Abounader, a professor at UVA's School of Medicine in the Department of Microbiology, Immunology and Cancer Biology, as well as its Comprehensive Cancer Center and Center for RNA Science and Medicine. "We are hoping to translate our findings into future clinical trials for patients with glioblastoma and other brain tumors."
paras.zh: UVA 医学院微生物学、免疫学和癌症生物学系以及综合癌症中心和 RNA 科学与医学中心的教授 Abounader 说：“这种新方法可以帮助靶向众多促进癌症生长的分子，包括那些尚无药物存在的分子，同时实现更好的治疗。” “我们希望将我们的发现转化为未来针对胶质母细胞瘤和其他脑肿瘤患者的临床试验。”

paras.en: Why Glioblastoma Is So Difficult to Treat
paras.zh: 为什么胶质母细胞瘤如此难以治疗

paras.en: Glioblastoma is the most common malignant brain tumor in adults and one of the most aggressive forms of cancer. It claims more than 13,000 lives in the United States each year. One reason it is so difficult to treat is that cancer cells spread into surrounding healthy brain tissue, making it nearly impossible for surgeons to remove the entire tumor.
paras.zh: 胶质母细胞瘤是成人最常见的恶性脑肿瘤，也是最具侵袭性的癌症之一。它每年在美国夺走超过 13,000 人的生命。治疗如此困难的原因之一是癌细胞扩散到周围健康的脑组织中，使得外科医生几乎不可能切除整个肿瘤。

paras.en: Another major challenge is the brain's natural "blood-brain barrier." This protective system helps shield the brain from harmful substances, including toxins and infectious agents. Unfortunately, it also blocks many drugs that could otherwise be used to attack brain cancer.
paras.zh: 另一个主要挑战是大脑天然的“血脑屏障”。这种保护系统有助于保护大脑免受有害物质的侵害，包括毒素和传染源。不幸的是，它还阻止了许多本来可以用来治疗脑癌的药物。

paras.en: Current treatment generally begins with surgery to remove as much of the tumor as possible. Patients then receive radiation therapy and chemotherapy to help control the remaining cancer and extend survival. Despite these efforts, glioblastoma remains exceptionally difficult to manage.
paras.zh: 目前的治疗通常从手术切除尽可能多的肿瘤开始。然后患者接受放射治疗和化学治疗，以帮助控制剩余的癌症并延长生存期。尽管做出了这些努力，胶质母细胞瘤仍然异常难以治疗。

paras.en: The UVA researchers are pursuing a different strategy. Instead of relying on drugs that target individual cancer-related processes, their approach uses microRNAs, small pieces of genetic material capable of suppressing the activity of multiple problematic genes at the same time.
paras.zh: 弗吉尼亚大学的研究人员正在采取不同的策略。他们的方法不是依赖针对个体癌症相关过程的药物，而是使用 microRNA，即能够同时抑制多个问题基因活性的小片段遗传物质。

paras.en: By disrupting several genes that help glioblastoma grow and survive, the treatment could potentially slow or even stop tumor growth. This ability to target multiple cancer-driving mechanisms is especially important because combining several conventional cancer drugs can produce harmful side effects. In addition, many of the molecules involved in cancer growth cannot currently be targeted by available medications.
paras.zh: 通过破坏一些有助于胶质母细胞瘤生长和存活的基因，这种治疗可能会减缓甚至阻止肿瘤的生长。这种针对多种癌症驱动机制的能力尤其重要，因为组合几种传统的癌症药物可能会产生有害的副作用。此外，目前可用的药物无法靶向许多与癌症生长有关的分子。

paras.en: Using Ultrasound to Deliver Cancer-Fighting Molecules
paras.zh: 使用超声波传递抗癌分子

paras.en: Getting these genetic molecules into the brain presents another major challenge. To overcome it, Abounader's team uses focused ultrasound guided by magnetic resonance imaging (MRI), allowing researchers to direct sound waves precisely toward the intended area.
paras.zh: 让这些遗传分子进入大脑是另一个重大挑战。为了克服这个问题，Abounader 的团队使用磁共振成像 (MRI) 引导的聚焦超声波，使研究人员能够将声波精确地引导到预期区域。

paras.en: The ultrasound works with tiny "microbubbles" to temporarily open the blood-brain barrier. This creates a brief opportunity for nanoparticles carrying the microRNAs to pass through the barrier and enter the brain, where they can act on genes involved in tumor growth.
paras.zh: 超声波与微小的“微泡”一起作用，暂时打开血脑屏障。这为携带 microRNA 的纳米粒子创造了短暂的机会穿过屏障并进入大脑，在那里它们可以作用于与肿瘤生长有关的基因。

paras.en: The researchers tested this approach in laboratory experiments and animal models of glioblastoma. Their findings showed that the microRNA treatment slowed tumor growth and helped the animals survive longer.
paras.zh: 研究人员在实验室实验和胶质母细胞瘤动物模型中测试了这种方法。他们的研究结果表明，microRNA 治疗可以减缓肿瘤生长并帮助动物存活更长时间。

paras.en: Although these results are encouraging, the strategy remains experimental and will require additional research before it can be evaluated in human patients. Abounader believes the findings provide an important early indication that the technology could eventually benefit people with glioblastoma and potentially those with other types of cancer.
paras.zh: 尽管这些结果令人鼓舞，但该策略仍处于试验阶段，需要进行更多研究才能在人类患者中进行评估。阿布纳德认为，这些发现提供了一个重要的早期迹象，表明该技术最终可能使胶质母细胞瘤患者以及其他类型癌症患者受益。

paras.en: "This approach could have broad applications for several brain and other human diseases," Abounader said. "We and many others are intensively working to lighten the burden of cancer, and hopefully also completely cure it, but this requires a continued investment in cancer and medical research."
paras.zh: “这种方法可以广泛应用于治疗多种大脑疾病和其他人类疾病，”阿布纳德说。 “我们和许多其他人正在加紧努力减轻癌症的负担，并希望也能彻底治愈它，但这需要对癌症和医学研究的持续投资。”

paras.en: UVA Expands Focused Ultrasound Cancer Research
paras.zh: UVA 扩大聚焦超声癌症研究

paras.en: UVA Health has been at the forefront of focused ultrasound research since the technology's early development. Over the years, its scientists have built an extensive research program investigating how precisely directed sound waves might be used to treat a wide range of medical conditions.
paras.zh: 自该技术早期开发以来，UVA Health 一直处于聚焦超声研究的前沿。多年来，科学家们建立了一个广泛的研究计划，研究如何使用精确定向的声波来治疗各种医疗状况。

paras.en: Recognizing the technology's potential in cancer care, UVA partnered with the Charlottesville-based Focused Ultrasound Foundation to establish the Focused Ultrasound Immuno-Oncology (FUSION) Center. It is the first center in the world devoted specifically to investigating how focused ultrasound can be combined with cancer immunotherapy. Researchers believe this combination could lead to major advances in cancer treatment during the 21st century.
paras.zh: 认识到该技术在癌症治疗方面的潜力，UVA 与位于夏洛茨维尔的聚焦超声基金会合作建立了聚焦超声免疫肿瘤学 (FUSION) 中心。它是世界上第一个专门致力于研究聚焦超声如何与癌症免疫疗法相结合的中心。研究人员相信，这种组合可能会导致 21 世纪癌症治疗的重大进展。

paras.en: The effort also supports the broader missions of UVA Comprehensive Cancer Center and UVA's Paul and Diane Manning Institute of Biotechnology, both of which are working to improve care through new medical discoveries.
paras.zh: 这项努力还支持弗吉尼亚大学综合癌症中心和弗吉尼亚大学保罗和黛安曼宁生物技术研究所的更广泛使命，这两家机构都致力于通过新的医学发现来改善护理。

paras.en: UVA Comprehensive Cancer Center is among just 57 cancer centers nationwide to receive the National Cancer Institute's prestigious "comprehensive" designation. The recognition reflects its excellence in cancer research and patient care.
paras.zh: UVA 综合癌症中心是全国仅有的 57 家获得国家癌症研究所著名的“综合”称号的癌症中心之一。该认可反映了其在癌症研究和患者护理方面的卓越表现。

paras.en: The Manning Institute was established to speed the discovery and development of new medicines and potential cures for some of the most difficult diseases. Its work is supported by a statewide clinical trials network designed to make emerging treatments more accessible to patients as they move through research and testing.
paras.zh: 曼宁研究所的成立是为了加速新药的发现和开发以及一些最棘手疾病的潜在治疗方法。其工作得到了全州临床试验网络的支持，该网络旨在使患者在研究和测试过程中更容易获得新兴治疗方法。

paras.en: Abounader and his colleagues published their experimental approach and initial laboratory findings in JCI, the Journal of Clinical Investigation. The study is open access and can be read free of charge.
paras.zh: Abounader 和他的同事在 JCI（《临床研究杂志》）上发表了他们的实验方法和初步实验室结果。该研究是开放获取的，可以免费阅读。

paras.en: The research team included Shekhar Saha, Ying Zhang, Myron K. articles.title: Drinking tea may help protect your heart, but there’s a surprising catch

paras.en: Drinking tea may help protect your heart, but thereâs a surprising catch
paras.zh: 喝茶可能有助于保护心脏，但有一个令人惊讶的收获

paras.en: - A massive study of nearly 486,000 adults found that regularly drinking tea was associated with an 11% lower risk of heart and blood vessel diseases. The lowest risk was linked to drinking roughly six to eight cups per day, with black tea showing more consistent benefits than green tea.
paras.zh: - 一项对近 486,000 名成年人进行的大规模研究发现，经常喝茶可使患心脏和血管疾病的风险降低 11%。风险最低的人每天喝大约六到八杯茶，红茶比绿茶显示出更一致的益处。

paras.en: Drinking tea regularly may offer important benefits for your heart and blood vessels, according to a massive study involving nearly 500,000 adults. Researchers found that people who consumed tea regularly had a lower risk of developing several vascular diseases compared with those who did not drink tea.
paras.zh: 一项涉及近 500,000 名成年人的大型研究表明，经常喝茶可能对您的心脏和血管有重要益处。研究人员发现，与不喝茶的人相比，经常喝茶的人患多种血管疾病的风险较低。

paras.en: However, the findings also revealed some unexpected differences. The type of tea, how strong it was, and even the temperature at which it was consumed were all associated with vascular health. While certain tea drinking habits were linked to a lower risk of disease, drinking tea at extremely high temperatures appeared to have the opposite association.
paras.zh: 然而，研究结果也揭示了一些意想不到的差异。茶的类型、浓度，甚至饮用温度都与血管健康有关。虽然某些饮茶习惯与较低的疾病风险有关，但在极高温度下喝茶似乎具有相反的关联。

paras.en: The research, published in the Journal of Internal Medicine, provides new insights into how an everyday beverage may be connected to long-term cardiovascular health.
paras.zh: 这项发表在《内科医学杂志》上的研究提供了关于日常饮料如何与长期心血管健康相关的新见解。

paras.en: Nearly 500,000 Adults Reveal a Link Between Tea and Vascular Health
paras.zh: 近 500,000 名成年人揭示了茶与血管健康之间的联系

paras.en: The study included 485,934 adults in China who were followed for a median of 9.05 years. During that period, researchers recorded 14,863 cases involving several types of vascular disease.
paras.zh: 该研究纳入了 485,934 名中国成年人，随访时间中位数为 9.05 年。在此期间，研究人员记录了 14,863 例涉及多种血管疾病的病例。

paras.en: These conditions included cardiovascular disease, which affects the heart and blood vessels, and cerebrovascular disease, which involves blood vessels that supply the brain. The researchers also examined pulmonary heart disease, a condition in which problems involving the lungs or their blood vessels place strain on the heart, and peripheral artery disease, which occurs when arteries carrying blood to areas such as the legs become narrowed or blocked.
paras.zh: 这些疾病包括心血管疾病（影响心脏和血管）和脑血管疾病（涉及供应大脑的血管）。研究人员还检查了肺心病（一种涉及肺部或其血管的问题对心脏造成压力的疾病）和外周动脉疾病（当输送血液到腿部等区域的动脉变窄或阻塞时就会发生这种疾病）。

paras.en: Although these conditions affect different parts of the body, they share an important feature: they interfere with the circulation of blood, which delivers oxygen and nutrients to organs and tissues.
paras.zh: 尽管这些病症影响身体的不同部位，但它们有一个重要特征：它们干扰血液循环，而血液循环向器官和组织输送氧气和营养物质。

paras.en: When the researchers compared tea drinking habits with the incidence of these diseases, they found that regular tea consumption was associated with an 11% lower risk of the combined vascular outcomes.
paras.zh: 当研究人员将饮茶习惯与这些疾病的发病率进行比较时，他们发现经常喝茶可以使综合血管疾病的风险降低 11%。

paras.en: The relationship also appeared to vary with the amount consumed. Among people who drank tea at least weekly, the lowest estimated risk occurred at approximately six to eight cups per day.
paras.zh: 这种关系似乎也随着消费量的变化而变化。在至少每周喝茶的人中，每天喝六到八杯茶的估计风险最低。

paras.en: This does not necessarily mean that drinking more tea directly prevents disease or that everyone should consume that amount. Because the research was observational, it could identify connections between tea drinking and health outcomes but could not establish that tea itself was responsible for the differences.
paras.zh: 这并不一定意味着多喝茶可以直接预防疾病，或者每个人都应该喝那么多茶。由于该研究是观察性的，因此它可以确定饮茶与健康结果之间的联系，但无法确定茶本身是造成这种差异的原因。

paras.en: Black Tea vs. Green Tea: Does the Type Matter?
paras.zh: 红茶与绿茶：类型重要吗？

paras.en: One particularly interesting finding involved the type of tea participants consumed.
paras.zh: 一项特别有趣的发现涉及参与者饮用的茶的类型。

paras.en: Black tea showed more consistent associations with a reduced risk of vascular disease than green tea. This suggests that different varieties of tea may not have identical relationships with cardiovascular health.
paras.zh: 与绿茶相比，红茶与降低血管疾病风险有更一致的关联。这表明不同品种的茶与心血管健康的关系可能不同。

paras.en: Both black and green tea come from the same plant, Camellia sinensis, but they undergo different processing methods. Black tea is typically allowed to undergo extensive oxidation, a chemical process that changes the composition of compounds in the leaves, while green tea is processed to limit oxidation.
paras.zh: 红茶和绿茶都来自同一种植物——茶树，但它们的加工方法不同。红茶通常会经历广泛的氧化，这是一种改变茶叶中化合物成分的化学过程，而绿茶则经过加工以限制氧化。

paras.en: Tea naturally contains plant compounds known as polyphenols, which have attracted scientific interest because of their antioxidant properties and potential effects on blood vessel function. Antioxidants can help limit certain types of cellular damage caused by reactive molecules.
paras.zh: 茶天然含有被称为多酚的植物化合物，由于其抗氧化特性和对血管功能的潜在影响而引起了科学界的兴趣。抗氧化剂可以帮助限制活性分子引起的某些类型的细胞损伤。

paras.en: However, the study does not establish whether these compounds explain the observed differences between black and green tea.
paras.zh: 然而，该研究并未确定这些化合物是否解释了红茶和绿茶之间观察到的差异。

paras.en: Tea strength also appeared to matter. Participants who drank tea of moderate strength had the lowest associated vascular disease risk, suggesting that stronger tea was not necessarily linked to greater benefits.
paras.zh: 茶的浓度似乎也很重要。喝中等浓度茶的参与者患血管疾病的风险最低，这表明浓度较高的茶不一定会带来更大的益处。

paras.en: Drinking Tea Too Hot May Carry Unexpected Risks
paras.zh: 喝太热的茶可能会带来意想不到的风险

paras.en: Perhaps the most surprising finding concerned tea temperature.
paras.zh: 也许最令人惊讶的发现与茶的温度有关。

paras.en: Although regular tea consumption was generally associated with a reduced risk of vascular disease, drinking tea described as "burning hot" was linked to an increased risk.
paras.zh: 虽然经常喝茶通常会降低患血管疾病的风险，但喝“热茶”会增加患血管疾病的风险。

paras.en: The result suggests that the temperature of tea may be an important consideration alongside how much people drink and which variety they prefer.
paras.zh: 结果表明，茶的温度可能是人们喝多少茶以及喜欢喝哪种茶的一个重要考虑因素。

paras.en: Very hot beverages can expose tissues in the mouth and digestive tract to high temperatures, but the study did not establish the biological mechanism behind the observed vascular risk. It also did not identify a specific temperature at which tea becomes harmful.
paras.zh: 非常热的饮料会使口腔和消化道的组织暴露在高温下，但该研究并未建立观察到的血管风险背后的生物学机制。它还没有确定茶变得有害的具体温度。

paras.en: The findings therefore should not be interpreted as proof that drinking extremely hot tea directly causes vascular disease. They do, however, raise questions about whether certain drinking habits could offset some of the favorable associations seen with regular tea consumption.
paras.zh: 因此，这一发现不应被解释为喝极热茶直接导致血管疾病的证据。然而，他们确实提出了这样的问题：某些饮酒习惯是否会抵消经常喝茶所带来的一些有利关联。

paras.en: Tea, Exercise, and Smoking Habits May Work Together
paras.zh: 喝茶、运动和吸烟的习惯可以一起发挥作用

paras.en: The researchers also examined how tea consumption related to other lifestyle factors, including smoking and physical activity.
paras.zh: 研究人员还研究了饮茶与其他生活方式因素（包括吸烟和体育活动）的关系。

paras.en: Their analysis showed that people who regularly drank tea, were not current smokers, and maintained high levels of physical activity had the lowest vascular disease risk.
paras.zh: 他们的分析表明，经常喝茶、不吸烟并且保持高水平体力活动的人患血管疾病的风险最低。

paras.en: "Joint analyses showed that tea consumption, smoking status and physical were collectively associated with vascular risk, with the favorable combination of habitual tea consumption, non-current smoking and high physical activity associated with the lowest risk," the authors wrote.
paras.zh: 作者写道：“联合分析表明，饮茶、吸烟状况和体力活动与血管风险共同相关，习惯性饮茶、不吸烟和高体力活动的有利组合与最低风险相关。”

paras.en: These results highlight the importance of considering overall lifestyle rather than looking at a single food or beverage in isolation.
paras.zh: 这些结果凸显了考虑整体生活方式而不是孤立地看待单一食物或饮料的重要性。

paras.en: Regular physical activity supports cardiovascular health in several ways, including improving circulation, helping regulate blood pressure, and supporting the function of the heart and blood vessels. Avoiding smoking also reduces exposure to substances that can damage blood vessels and increase cardiovascular risk.
paras.zh: 定期的体育活动可以通过多种方式支持心血管健康，包括改善血液循环、帮助调节血压以及支持心脏和血管的功能。避免吸烟还可以减少接触可能损害血管并增加心血管风险的物质。

paras.en: Taken together, the findings suggest that tea drinking may be one component of a broader pattern of habits associated with better vascular health.
paras.zh: 总而言之，研究结果表明，喝茶可能是与更好的血管健康相关的更广泛的习惯模式的一个组成部分。

paras.en: Although more research is needed to determine whether tea consumption directly influences disease risk, the study offers encouraging evidence that this widely consumed beverage is associated with cardiovascular health. It also highlights an important distinction: when it comes to tea, the amount, variety, strength, and temperature may all be worth considering.
paras.zh: 尽管还需要更多的研究来确定喝茶是否直接影响疾病风险，但该研究提供了令人鼓舞的证据，证明这种广泛饮用的饮料与心血管健康有关。它还强调了一个重要的区别：当谈到茶时，数量、品种、浓度和温度可能都值得考虑。

articles.title: The Great Barrier Reef's most notorious coral killer may actually be helping it

paras.en: The Great Barrier Reef's most notorious coral killer may actually be helping it

- Crown-of-thorns starfish are notorious for devouring coral reefs, but surprising new research reveals these spiny predators may actually help reefs thrive when their populations are kept in check. Scientists studying Australia's Great Barrier Reef discovered that nearly 75% of observed starfish feeding events left behind living coral tissue, rather than destroying entire colonies. By feeding on fast-growing, dominant corals, the starfish create opportunities for slower-growing species to survive, potentially increasing coral biodiversity.
paras.zh: QUERY LENGTH LIMIT EXCEEDED. MAX ALLOWED QUERY : 500 CHARS

paras.en: Crown-of-thorns starfish (COTS) are among the most feared creatures on coral reefs. Covered in sharp, toxin-filled spines, these predators are notorious for consuming coral and leaving widespread destruction in their wake.

However, new research from the University of Sydney suggests these infamous reef destroyers may also have a surprisingly beneficial side. When their populations remain under control, crown-of-thorns starfish can help maintain healthy coral communities and support greater biodiversity.

Native to Australia's Great Barrier Reef, these coral-eating starfish have caused enormous damage during population explosions. Since the 1960s, the reef has experienced four major outbreaks, occurring roughly every 15 years. Declining numbers of natural predators, including tritons and several species of reef fish, have made the Great Barrier Reef and other marine ecosystems more vulnerable to these destructive events.
Scientists Discover That Coral Often Survives Starfish Attacks

In a study published in Ecology and Evolution, researchers investigated what happens to coral after crown-of-thorns starfish feed on it. The team examined feeding scars and remaining living tissue at the University of Sydney's One Tree Island Research Station, located on the Great Barrier Reef.

The study sites were within protected areas where healthy fish populations help keep starfish numbers under control. Unlike other parts of the reef that experience devastating outbreaks, these locations maintain relatively low populations of crown-of-thorns starfish.
The results revealed an unexpected pattern. A team led by Dr. Shawna Foo found that living coral tissue survived nearly 75 percent of the observed feeding events.

"At One Tree Reef, COTS appear to consume a relatively consistent amount of coral during each meal and move on, rather than demolishing the entire coral colony," said Dr. Foo, a University of Sydney Horizon Fellow in the School of Life and Environmental Sciences. "This meant live coral tissue remnants were frequently left behind."
How Coral-Eating Starfish Can Boost Reef Biodiversity
The discovery suggests that small populations of crown-of-thorns starfish may play an important role in maintaining the balance of coral reef ecosystems.

Some coral species grow quickly and can take over large areas, limiting the space available to slower-growing varieties. By feeding on these dominant species, crown-of-thorns starfish may create opportunities for other corals to survive and establish themselves.

The researchers found that surviving fragments of fast-growing Acroporidae corals did not regenerate over the areas damaged by starfish feeding. In contrast, regrowth occurred primarily among slower-growing Montipora and Porites corals.
"By feeding on fast-growing corals such as Acropora, low-density COTS populations create space for slower-growing coral species to persist, helping to increase coral diversity," Dr. Foo said.

This finding challenges the idea that all coral consumption by crown-of-thorns starfish is harmful. Under the right conditions, their feeding behavior may actually prevent a few dominant coral species from taking over the reef.
Why Eliminating Crown-of-Thorns Starfish Could Be a Mistake

Despite these potential benefits, researchers caution that large outbreaks of crown-of-thorns starfish remain a serious threat. When their numbers increase dramatically, they can destroy extensive areas of coral, leaving reefs struggling to recover.
The key difference is whether starfish populations remain at naturally manageable levels or grow into destructive outbreaks.
"It's important to distinguish between COTS populations performing their natural role as coral predators and outbreaks causing sustained reef decline."

Although the research was conducted mainly in protected areas with healthy fish populations and little risk of major outbreaks, the findings could help scientists and conservation managers improve strategies for controlling crown-of-thorns starfish.
In particular, the results suggest that removing every starfish may not be the best approach once an outbreak has been brought under control.
paras.zh: 特别是，结果表明，一旦疫情得到控制，清除所有海星可能并不是最好的方法。

paras.en: "The implications of our work can help us decide when and why culling should occur and the ecological endpoint of a cull. Once an outbreak is suppressed, the goal should not necessarily be to eliminate COTS entirely. Culling needs to be complemented by strong marine management to protect COTS predators and keep COTS populations in check."
Research co-author Professor Maria Byrne connected the findings to a well-established ecological concept.
paras.zh: 研究合著者玛丽亚·伯恩教授将这些发现与一个完善的生态概念联系起来。

paras.en: "The results are consistent with the intermediate disturbance hypothesis, an important framework in ecology and conservation."
According to this hypothesis, ecosystems can benefit from occasional, moderate disturbances that prevent any single species from becoming too dominant.
paras.zh: 根据这一假设，生态系统可以从偶尔的、适度的干扰中受益，这些干扰可以防止任何单一物种变得过于占主导地位。

paras.en: The research suggests that crown-of-thorns starfish may be an example of this natural balancing process. While uncontrolled outbreaks can devastate coral reefs, smaller populations may help maintain the diversity that makes these ecosystems so valuable.
paras.zh: 研究表明，棘冠海星可能是这种自然平衡过程的一个例子。虽然不受控制的爆发可能会摧毁珊瑚礁，但较小的种群数量可能有助于维持使这些生态系统变得如此有价值的多样性。

paras.zh: 材料由悉尼大学提供。注意：内容可能会根据样式和长度进行编辑。

articles.title: 5 bright planets to spot in November — when and where to see them
articles.author: Joe Rao

paras.en: This is a great month for planet watching, either in the evenings or mornings. During convenient evening hours, the planet of choice is Saturn, visible well up in the southern sky during mid-to-late evening hours. Telescopically, the southern side of its famous ring system is currently tilted about 6½ degrees to our line of sight.

Around the middle of the night, Mars and Jupiter come into view above the east-northeast horizon and just before the break of dawn are in excellent position, soaring high in the southern sky in the vicinity of the Sickle of Leo the Lion. Watch how Mars approaches Jupiter early in the month, passes it on Nov. 16, then spends the rest of the month sailing away to the east.

Meanwhile, in the predawn morning sky, Venus literally vaults into prominence as the month progresses. And from midmonth on through the end of November, Mercury asserts itself, appearing as a very bright "star" to the far lower left of Venus.

In our schedule, remember that when measuring the angular separation between two celestial objects, your clenched fist held at arm's length measures roughly 10 degrees. Here, we present a schedule below which provides some of the best planet viewing times as well directing you as to where to look to see them

Reminder: On Nov. 1 — where applicable — change clocks back one hour from Daylight Saving Time. On this date, the clock hour from 1 to 2:00 a.m. is repeated, thus making this day the longest of the year: 25 hours long. The mnemonic is: "Spring Ahead, Fall Back."

Mercury, hidden during inferior conjunction with the sun on Nov. 4, will emerge in the eastern morning sky after the second week of the month to undergo an excellent morning apparition for the Northern Hemisphere. This rocky little world arrives at its greatest western elongation (20 degrees) from the sun on Nov. 20; its most favorable morning apparition of the year for mid-northern observers. From Nov. 16 to Nov. 26 speedy Mercury will rise in the east-southeast before the beginning of astronomical twilight, more than 95 minutes before sunrise.
paras.zh: QUERY LENGTH LIMIT EXCEEDED. MAX ALLOWED QUERY : 500 CHARS

paras.en: Venus is a good reason to be up at the crack of dawn in November; it's a silvery lamp that rises above the east-southeast horizon. Venus was at inferior conjunction on Oct. 24. But the steep angle of the ecliptic at dawn in late autumn helps Venus vault noticeably higher with each passing day for observers at mid-northern latitudes. On Nov. 1, it rises 55 minutes before the sun. But just several days later on Nov. 5, viewers around 40 degrees north latitude can see Venus come up one hour and 25 minutes before the sun and shine 15 degrees above the horizon at sunrise. As November ends, Venus rises nearly 3½ hours before the sun and hangs nearly 35 degrees up at sunrise.
paras.zh: QUERY LENGTH LIMIT EXCEEDED. MAX ALLOWED QUERY : 500 CHARS

paras.en: All month Venus brightens impressively and on the penultimate day of the month it will reach the pinnacle of its magnificent brightness, shining at magnitude -4.9, rising almost 3½ hours before the sun. If there's snow on the ground, check for shadows made by Venus's light. Through a telescope, the phase of the planet looks most remarkable early in the month. That's when you may be able to glimpse Venus when it's only a few percent illuminated, a hairline crescent close to an arcminute long; about 1/30 the apparent diameter of the moon. Venus is not alone in the dawn sky.
paras.zh: QUERY LENGTH LIMIT EXCEEDED. MAX ALLOWED QUERY : 500 CHARS

paras.en: Its leap takes it up into the proximity of the bluish 1st-magnitude star Spica in Virgo on the morning of Nov. 3. The star will be sitting 2.4 degrees to the upper right of Venus. During this month, Venus seems to perform a dos-à-dos with Spica and at first seems destined to soar up and catch it. Instead, the closest it gets to this star is 1.8 degrees to its upper left early on the morning of Nov. 19.

On the morning of Nov. 7, a striking array of a waning crescent moon, brilliant Venus and Spica awaits early risers low in the east-southeast sky about an hour before sunrise. The trio will be bunched together inside of a circle measuring only about 2½ degrees in diameter.

Mars, shining at magnitude +0.9, is in Leo in the morning sky and is easily found on the morning of Nov. 2, using the moon as a guide. That day it sits a couple of degrees to the left of the moon. In addition, on that date, Mars is positioned 5 degrees to the upper right of much brighter Jupiter.

Mars has been hiding in the glare of the sun, or in the dead of the early morning hours, for the last year and a quarter. Now it finally rises in the east before midnight. Each night, watch the orange-yellow planet move a little closer to Jupiter. They'll be in conjunction on Nov. 16 (See Jupiter below).

On the morning of Nov. 26, Mars, having brightened to magnitude +0.6, passes 1.7 degrees to the upper left of the first magnitude star Regulus in Leo. The color contrast between the orange-yellow planet and blue-white star is striking, especially in binoculars.
Jupiter is high enough for a steady telescopic view by 3 a.m. But its dusky cloud belts and Red Spot can be seen more clearly when the planet is highest in the southeast soon after dawn breaks.

On Nov. 3, shortly after 1 a.m. local time, look low toward the east-northeast horizon to watch the moon slowly ascend the sky. The 1st magnitude star Regulus will be evident sitting a degree to the moon's left. And sitting about 5 degrees above the moon will be Jupiter, appearing as a brilliant "star" shining with a steady, silvery light.

Mars passes 1.2 degrees to the upper left of Jupiter on Nov. 16; the giant planet outshining the red planet 13-fold. Late on Nov. 29 and into the early hours of Nov. 30, look low toward the east-northeast horizon for a gathering of the waning gibbous moon, with Jupiter, Regulus and Mars. These four celestial bodies cover an expanse of roughly 7 degrees going from right to left. Best views will come around the time of the break of dawn when they'll appear to soar high in the southern sky.

Saturn is situated in the northeast corner of the non-zodiacal constellation of Cetus the Whale (or Sea Monster). It crosses the southern meridian around 9:45 p.m. at the beginning of November and about two hours earlier at the month's end. All evening, it is excellently placed for telescopic viewing of its glorious ball and rings. At magnitude +0.6, Saturn is easily the brightest point of light in its section of the heavens. It can also be told from the stars by its steady, yellowish light.
On the evening of Nov. 18, take note of Saturn mimicking a bright "star" shining about 6 degrees below the waxing gibbous moon.

Joe Rao serves as an instructor and guest lecturer at New York's Hayden Planetarium. He writes about astronomy for Natural History magazine, Sky and Telescope, The Old Farmer's Almanac and other publications.

Joe Rao is Space.com's skywatching columnist, as well as a veteran meteorologist and eclipse chaser who also serves as an instructor and guest lecturer at New York's Hayden Planetarium. He writes about astronomy for Natural History magazine, Sky & Telescope and other publications. Joe is an 8-time Emmy-nominated meteorologist who served the Putnam Valley region of New York for over 21 years. You can find him on Twitter and YouTube tracking lunar and solar eclipses, meteor showers and more. To find out Joe's latest project, visit him on Twitter.

articles.title: NASA's Swift space telescope is about to crash to Earth. Where will it fall?
articles.author: Leonard David

paras.en: NASA's Swift space telescope is expected to crash back to Earth in the next few days.
The Neil Gehrels Swift Observatory will reenter Earth's atmosphere in an uncontrolled fashion, after a robotic rescue mission failed to boost the scope to a higher orbit.

Swift launched to Earth orbit back in November 2004. Over the next two decades, it studied gamma-ray bursts — the most powerful explosions in the universe — and other cosmic objects and events using a trio of telescopes: a Burst Alert Telescope (BAT), an X-Ray Telescope (XRT), and its Ultraviolet/Optical Telescope (UVOT).

On Oct. 20, NASA reported that Swift's orbit had decayed to 171 miles (275 kilometers) above Earth and that the roughly 3,300-pound (1,500-kilogram) observatory was no longer able to compensate for the effects of the increased drag. It entered safe mode, followed by Swift's operations team at Pennsylvania State University sending a command to the spacecraft that effectively ended its operations ahead of its destructive and fiery nose-dive.
It's unclear at the moment exactly when and where Swift will plunge to Earth. But researchers definitely have their eyes peeled.
In physics fashion, for the most part, what goes up must come down — with more space hardware to follow.

Thanks to the growing surge in low Earth orbit constellations and technology refresh cycles, there are 10 times more objects reentering per year than there were just five years ago, said Darren McKnight, a senior technical fellow at LeoLabs, a company that keeps a watchful eye on what's going on above our planet.

"It is unfortunate that Swift was not 'reorbited,' but from a reentry hazard perspective it is a small portion of the stuff coming back in. The rub on this, of course, is that, while many people bemoan the reentry of more objects, I am much more upset about the rapid rate of abandoning massive objects above 400 miles [644 km]," McKnight told Space.com.

Swift will likely disintegrate sufficiently upon reentry to not pose a ground casualty hazard, McKnight said. However, the internal workings of the observatory's X-ray and optical telescope might survive, McKnight said.
Similar in view is Dean Sladen, a quality manager and aerospace engineer at the U.K. precision-components supplier Accu Components.

"Once Swift falls to about 120 kilometers [75 miles], the end usually comes within a few minutes. The air in front of it heats up so much that the satellite will start to glow. Solar panels and antennas are typically the first to tear off, and at around 78 kilometers [48 miles], roughly eight times the height of a passing airliner, the main body breaks apart. Most of it will melt and vaporize," said Sladen.
While it isn't yet known exactly where any surviving pieces will land, Sladen noted that Swift's orbit only passes over a band within about 21 degrees of the equator.
"That band is mostly ocean, though it also crosses populated parts of Africa, South and Southeast Asia and Latin America," he said.

As for which parts are most likely to survive and reach ocean or ground, Sladen pointed out that most of Swift's body is aluminum, wiring and electronics, which melt away early in the reentry process. What reaches Earth is usually small, dense and heat-resistant, such as titanium, steel and glass.

"The most likely survivors are its six heavy reaction wheels, the spinning flywheels it used to aim itself, along with tougher telescope parts such as lenses and mirrors. Its mask of around 52,000 tiny lead tiles will almost certainly melt. Only a handful of small, scorched fragments are expected to make it down — nothing recognizable as a telescope," Sladen said.
Sladen said that, at the current time, it appears that no detailed risk assessment has been published for Swift's fall.
"However, this does not mean NASA has not done the work," said Sladen.

"NASA's own orbital debris requirements state that the risk of human casualty from surviving debris shall not exceed one in 10,000, so it is highly likely this work has been completed but not published," he told Space.com. "Personally, I believe it should be published, as NASA has done with previous satellites. The risk is almost certainly very small, but it would give people a clear, factual picture rather than guesswork."
Sladen added that there's far more focus on how a satellite's life ends these days than there was in the past.

"Many now carry enough propulsion to steer themselves into a remote stretch of ocean, or are built from materials designed to burn up completely, an approach called 'design for demise.' NASA and the European Space Agency limit the chance of anyone being hurt by a reentry to one in 10,000, and if a satellite can't meet that, it's expected to come down in a controlled way," said Sladen.
So, should people be worried about having a nasty run-in with Swift leftovers?

Sladen doesn't think so. NASA has said that harm to anyone on the ground is unlikely, and LeoLabs also describes the risk as very small. Most of the spacecraft will burn up, and any surviving pieces will most likely fall into the sea, he said.

"The real concern is the long-term trend. With more satellites being launched than ever, the number of uncontrolled reentries is growing, which is why designing satellites to come down safely matters more and more," Sladen concluded.

Leonard David is an award-winning space journalist who has been reporting on space activities for more than 50 years. Currently writing as Space.com's Space Insider Columnist among his other projects, Leonard has authored numerous books on space exploration, Mars missions and more, with his latest being "Moon Rush: The New Space Race" published in 2019 by National Geographic. He also wrote "Mars: Our Future on the Red Planet" released in 2016 by National Geographic. Leonard has served as a correspondent for SpaceNews, Scientific American and Aerospace America for the AIAA. He has received many awards, including the first Ordway Award for Sustained Excellence in Spaceflight History in 2015 at the AAS Wernher von Braun Memorial Symposium. You can find out Leonard's latest project at his website and on Twitter.

articles.title: 'The Sea God Surveys': Watch Rocket Lab launch Japanese Earth-observing satellite today
articles.author: Mike Wall

paras.en: Rocket Lab will launch its 99th mission to date today (Nov. 2), and you can watch the action live.
An Electron rocket is scheduled to lift off from Rocket Lab's New Zealand site today, during a window that opens at 11:30 a.m. EST (1630 GMT; 5:30 a.m. on Nov. 3 local New Zealand time),

The mission, which Rocket Lab calls "The Sea God Surveys," will carry an Earth-observing radar satellite for the Japanese company iQPS. You can watch it live via Rocket Lab starting about 30 minutes before launch, and Space.com will carry the company's feed if, as expected, it's made available.
"The Sea God Surveys" will be Rocket Lab's 10th launch to date for iQPS, which is assembling a constellation of three dozen synthetic aperture radar (SAR) satellites in low Earth orbit (LEO).
SAR satellites offer advantages over those that view our planet in optical wavelengths. They can peer through cloud cover, for example, and study our planet at night as well as during the day.

Today's launch will be the 99th overall for Rocket Lab and the 90th for the two-stage, 59-foot-tall (18 meters) Electron, which gives small satellites dedicated rides to space. The workhorse vehicle has already flown 16 times this year.

Rocket Lab's other nine launches to date have been conducted by HASTE, a suborbital version of Electron that allows customers to test their tech in the hypersonic flight environment. HASTE (short for "Hypersonic Accelerator Suborbital Test Electron") debuted in June 2023 and generally flies classified payloads.

Michael Wall is the Spaceflight and Tech Editor for Space.com and joined the team in 2010. He primarily covers human and robotic spaceflight, military space, and exoplanets, but has been known to dabble in the space art beat. His book about the search for alien life, "Out There," was published on Nov. 13, 2018. Before becoming a science writer, Michael worked as a herpetologist and wildlife biologist. He has a Ph.D. in evolutionary biology from the University of Sydney, Australia, a bachelor's degree from the University of Arizona, and a graduate certificate in science writing from the University of California, Santa Cruz. To find out what his latest project is, you can follow Michael on Twitter.
